subject.title: fix(qa): reject runtime tool intent without result evidence

question: Should required OpenClaw/Codex runtime-tool release coverage intentionally be limited to the three result-backed rows (`session-status`, `web-fetch`, and `web-search`), with the other nine previously required rows retained only as non-required diagnostics?
rationale: The patch correctly distinguishes actual result-backed execution from intent or report-only evidence, but choosing which tools constitute the release-readiness floor is a maintainer-owned QA policy decision.

options.title: Approve the three-tool baseline
options.body: Land the PR with `session-status`, `web-fetch`, and `web-search` as the explicit required result-backed runtime-tool coverage contract.

options.title: Require additional result-backed rows first
options.body: Keep the PR open and identify which demoted tools must gain canonical call/result fixtures before their required status can be removed.

options.title: Split policy from mechanics
options.body: Land only the honest pass/fail/skip and result-linking mechanics in a narrower patch, then decide required-row policy in a dedicated QA contract change.

recommendation.title: Approve the three-tool baseline
recommendation.body: Land the PR with `session-status`, `web-fetch`, and `web-search` as the explicit required result-backed runtime-tool coverage contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged persisted-evidence work establishes the collector and coverage contract this PR extends.
